title: AI热潮席卷美国高校 学生创业生态升温
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: So there's this growing debate over whether college is still worth it in the age of AI.
segments.zh: 如今，关于大学在AI时代是否还值得读，争论日益升温。

segments.en: It's the technology friends to reshape entry-level jobs in particular, but on college campuses, there's another side to the story.
segments.zh: 这项技术尤其重塑了入门级工作，但在大学校园里，故事还有另一面。

segments.en: A kind of AI gold rush, fueling a new generation of student founders.
segments.zh: 一场AI淘金热，正催生新一代学生创业者。

segments.en: A Molly Fowler is the founding partner at dorm room fund, which backs students and recent graduates.
segments.zh: 莫莉·福勒是Dorm Room Fund的创始合伙人，该基金支持学生和应届毕业生。

segments.en: And in very simple terms, that is what you're doing.
segments.zh: 简单来说，这就是你们在做的事。

segments.en: You are finding the start-up or the idea.
segments.zh: 你们在寻找初创公司或创意。

segments.en: Maybe in some cases where the student is still on campus, still studying.
segments.zh: 有时学生还在校园里，还在读书。

segments.en: That's an interesting strategy. Explain how it works.
segments.zh: 这策略挺有意思。解释一下怎么运作。

segments.en: Yeah, sure thing, Ed. So this is not necessarily such a crazy idea as it used to be 14 years ago when we started.
segments.zh: 好的，Ed。14年前我们起步时，这想法还没现在这么疯狂。

segments.en: But dorm room funds thesis is that when there are massive technology shifts, it creates this really interesting environment where the sort of macro trends
segments.zh: 但Dorm Room Fund的核心理念是，当技术发生大规模变革时，会创造出非常有趣的环境，宏观趋势……

segments.en: privilege first-time builders and folks that are on campus.
segments.zh: 优先考虑首次创业者和校园里的人。

segments.en: Yes. It's sort of a result of the fact that if you think about it, university campuses are in a lot of ways the ultimate hacker house or accelerator.
segments.zh: 是的。这某种程度上是因为，大学校园在很多方面就是终极黑客空间或加速器。

segments.en: You know, it's a concentration of talent. They've got time to build.
segments.zh: 你知道，这里人才集中，他们有时间去构建。

segments.en: Teachers teaching them the cutting edges of the bleeding edge of technology.
segments.zh: 老师教他们最前沿的技术。

segments.en: And they've got a ton of just incredible humans around them to help them build.
segments.zh: 而且他们周围有很多了不起的人帮助他们构建。

segments.en: And so as we thought about this back in 2012, when the cloud compute revolution was new, we thought to ourselves, gosh, we need to find a really effective way to figure out who's great.
segments.zh: 所以当我们在2012年思考这个问题时，云计算革命刚刚兴起，我们想，天哪，我们需要找到一种真正有效的方法来找出谁很棒。

segments.en: And who might just be sort of feeling things out for a class project.
segments.zh: 以及谁可能只是在为课堂项目摸索。
